meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'глашать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to invite', paired with 'пригласить'.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'God, god' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agreeing; consonant').

examples.text: Я их продам и куплю тебе приставку. Ну, согласен?
examples.trans: I'll sell it and buy you a console. Well, deal?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'actress' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She wants to become an actress.
A famous stage and film actress.

examples.text: Я буду работать официанткой. Буду ходить по кастингам и стану актрисой.
examples.trans: I will work as a waitress. I'll go to auditions and become an actress.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree, to arrange', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to kiss', paired with 'поцеловать'.

examples.trans: Well, call me, kitten. Bye, kisses!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бронировать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reserve, book', paired with 'бронировать'.

examples.text: Макс решил забронировать столик на вечер.
examples.trans: Max decided to reserve a table for the evening.

examples.text: Алло, ресторан, я хочу забронировать столик.
examples.trans: Hello, restaurant, I want to reserve a table.
Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small table, café table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to book, reserve'.

examples.text: Он каждый день его бронирует и не приходит.
examples.trans: He reserves it every single day and never shows up.

examples.text: Он его на сегодня уже забронировал.
examples.trans: He has already reserved it for tonight.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come', paired with 'прийти'.

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we will finish talking'.

related.gloss: to we will finish talking (prefixed perfective)
not to we will finish talking (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Тихо, мы с тобой потом договорим.
examples.trans: Quiet, you and I will finish talking later.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и договорить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will finish talking on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

examples.text: О чём предупреждал? Да ты что делаешь?
examples.trans: Warned me about what? Hey, what are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fifth').

examples.trans: The guest at table five is waiting.
Who is sitting at the fifth table?
Nastya, quickly clear the fifth table!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'только'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: There are so many mistakes there!
I don't have that much time.

examples.text: Там столько ошибок! Мы же всё быстро делали.
examples.trans: There are so many mistakes there! After all, we did everything in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказать'.

examples.text: Ладно, звони в свою пиццу. Заказывай!
examples.trans: All right, call your pizza place. Go ahead and order!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'as if, as though', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'post, office' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он идёт на пост мэра города.
examples.trans: He is running for the post of mayor of the city.

examples.text: Он выдвигает свою кандидатуру на пост мэра города!
examples.trans: He is putting forward his candidacy for the post of mayor of the city!

examples.text: Тебя всерьёз рассматривают на пост министра.
examples.trans: They are seriously considering you for the post of minister.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to end, to be over', paired with 'заканчиваться'.

examples.text: Всё, выборы закончились. Тебя начальник ждёт.
examples.trans: That's it, the election is over. Your boss is waiting for you.
